messages:
alice-support: heads up — we got a high-severity support escalation from Acme. Intermittent 401s on every API call since they rotated their OIDC provider keys last night. Error in logs: `jwt: signature verification failed` and `no matching JWK for kid`. Repro steps they sent below.

alice-support: repro steps from customer (copied):
1) obtain token from acme-idp at 2024-06-02T22:13:00Z
2) call our `/v1/generate` endpoint with that bearer token
3) see 401 with body `{"error":"invalid_token","reason":"signature_error"}`

alice-support: logs they attached (sanitized):
```
2024-06-02T22:13:05Z ERROR auth.jwt validate.go:87 signature verification failed kid=abc123 token_aud=redwood-api
2024-06-02T22:13:05Z DEBUG auth.jwks cache.go:56 jwks cached_at=2024-06-02T22:08:00Z ttl=300s url=https://acme-idp/.well-known/jwks.json
2024-06-02T22:13:05Z INFO proxy.req handler.go:210 request_id=xyz-789 status=401
```

alice-support: they mentioned the idp rotates keys every hour and their tokens contain `nbf` about +90s into the future (their client clock is slightly skewed).

alice-support: @devon-eng can you take a look? Sounds like JWKS caching + clock skew edge case. :eyes:

devon-eng: looking. couple quick questions — do they see `no matching JWK for kid` or `signature verification failed`? Those are different.

alice-support: both — sometimes `no matching JWK for kid` then after a minute `signature verification failed`. Attached base64 header from token: `eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6ImFiYzEyMyJ9` (decodes to `{"alg":"RS256","kid":"abc123"}`).

devon-eng: thanks. preliminary hypothesis: their idp rotated keys and published new JWKS; our runtime is caching the old JWKS and continues to validate against it. When we do a refresh, it sometimes sees the old key set due to upstream CDN caching or our cache TTL. Also their token `nbf` +90s could trigger `token not yet valid` if our clock skew tolerance is low.

sanjay-sre: adding infra detail — our JWKS cache TTL currently is 5m and we refresh proactively only every TTL or when we hit a 401 with `kid not found` path. There's a known bug where the refresh-on-401 only triggers for `signature verification failed` but the code path that checks `kid` returns early and doesn't trigger refresh. Filed a note in diag logs: `jwks: early return no kid match` but we didn't call fetch.

kim-security: this is a classic race: idp rotates, some tokens still valid, but our cached keys stale. Also clock skew is common — we historically tolerated 60s. If client `nbf` is +90s, that will fail. We should increase skew tolerance and make JWKS handling more robust.

paul-platform: two-pronged fix suggestion:
- short term: add an emergency ops workaround: set jwks_cache_ttl=30s for the affected region/tenant and flip logs to debug so we can monitor refreshes.
- medium term: patch runtime to call `fetch_jwks()` whenever `kid` in token header is not found in cache (currently we don't for performance reasons). Also add a resilient backoff and background refresh after failed fetch to avoid stampedes.

devon-eng: agree. also add these mitigations: bump clock skew tolerance to 300s (5m) configurable per-tenant, and log the token header `kid` + jwks cached_at for every auth failure so we can do triage faster.

alice-support: customer wants an ETA — they are in production and this is affecting ~80% of their requests. Can we do the short-term workaround now?

paul-platform: I can patch the runtime config on their dedicated pool to set jwks_cache_ttl=30 and enable immediate refresh-on-401 for that pool. Will do but need approval to push change to dedicated clusters.

kim-security: +1 from security. Need to ensure we don't create a DoS risk on idp endpoints. Add a rate limit on JWKS fetches per tenant (e.g., 1 fetch per 5s with exponential backoff on failure).

sanjay-sre: deploy-bot kicked off a canary change to update jwks cache ttl in prod for the dedicated cluster. See job: `deploy-bot: canary INF-1234-jwks-refresh`.

deploy-bot: canary started for cluster redwood-dedicated-acme-1. Rolling 2 pods, verifying auth health checks.

devon-eng: small note on signature errors: there are cases where alg confusion causes `signature verification failed` — e.g., token header alg=HS256 but idp signs with RS256. Confirming customer's header is RS256. If we ever see `alg` mismatch we should reject and log both alg and expected alg.

alice-support: customer also shared a curl they used to fetch JWKS: `curl -s -D - https://acme-idp/.well-known/jwks.json | head` — they saw a Cache-Control: max-age=600 header from upstream CDN. That explains why even after rotation clients saw old keys.

devon-eng: action items I'm taking now:
1) add an immediate short-term hotfix to trigger fetch_jwks() when `kid` not found (no codepath early return).
2) add enhanced logging: log token header `kid`, `alg`, local cached jwks `cached_at`, and the HTTP status from jwks endpoint.
3) add configurable clock-skew tolerance default 300s.
4) include rate-limiter on jwks fetch (1 fetch/10s per tenant default).
I'll open PR and attach test coverage.

kim-security: please include a unit test simulating JWKS rotate + stale CDN cache where fetch returns same body for first X attempts, then new key. Also an integration test to simulate tokens with `nbf` 2m in future to ensure tolerance works.

paul-platform: ops workaround applied to Acme cluster: jwks_cache_ttl=30s, refresh_on_401=true, fetch-rate-limit=1/5s. Monitoring: added alert for >5% auth failures over 1m.

alice-support: customer confirms partial recovery after our change — error rate dropped from ~85% to ~12% in first 10 minutes. They still see occasional 401s when their client clock is ~90s fast.

devon-eng: will prioritize the PR. Tentative timeline: hotfix branch + tests today, roll to canary tonight, full rollout tomorrow morning. Ticket INF-1234 updated.

kim-security: after rollout let's run a short audit: extract token header `kid` histogram over 24h and correlate with jwks fetch times, then we can fine-tune cache_ttl and rate limits.

alice-support: thanks everyone. I'll keep Acme updated and will post follow-ups here. :party-parrot: 

paul-platform: note for postmortem: add documentation for tenants about idp rotation best practices (publish old keys for a grace period, set small cdn max-age on jwks endpoints, avoid future `nbf` usage).

devon-eng: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/inference/pulls/987 — includes fix + tests. Please review.

sanjay-sre: canary metrics look stable after 30m, auth failure alert tripped once during a spike but recovered. Scheduling full rollout in 2h.

alice-support: marking as resolved with ongoing monitoring; will reopen if customer reports more problems.

kim-security: postmortem owner? devon-eng volunteer.

devon-eng: happy to own postmortem and follow-up improvements (INF-1250 backlog).
